newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa helps destroy Mozambican arms caches.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa helps destroy Mozambican arms caches.

text.p: Mozambique and South Africa seized and destroyed thousands of weapons and millions of rounds of ammunition in a three-week operation in Mozambique, South African police said on Monday.
The operation was launched to locate the large number of arms caches which still exist in the formerly Marxist-led country emerging from 16 years of ruinous civil war.

South African Police Director Reg Crewe said in a statement that firearms and other weapons were smuggled into South Africa from Mozambique and subsequently used in armed robberies, car-jackings and other crimes.
"These arms caches had to be lifted and destroyed in order to stabilise the crime situation in both countries," he added.

Crewe said the weapons found and destroyed included more than 5,500 machineguns, sub-machineguns and automatic rifles, 336 hand-grenades, 3,726 mortar bombs, 79 rocket and mortar launchers and tubes and about three million rounds of ammunition of various calibres.

"This should have a positive impact on the flow of illegal weapons across our border," he said. "It is envisaged that similar types of operations will be conducted in future, and may even be broadened."

South Africa and Mozambique have a bilateral agreement on crime prevention. The two governments are also cooperating to build a development corridor linking Johannesburg with Maputo, its nearest port and Mozambique's capital.
